transcript: Hello from the fourth preview of Galileo. This is my first time seeing this on Broadway, but my second time seeing Galileo after seeing the first preview of the Berkeley version. And they have changed so much of this from Berkeley to Broadway. The biggest change is giving Virginia, Galileo's daughter, a lot more material, which is absolutely the right decision when you have Joy Woods playing her, Incredibly, absolutely stopping the show multiple times. Worth the price of admission just to see freaking Joy Woods rock this show. They have also done a lot of changes to the writing. I feel like a lot of lyrics got changed from the Berkeley version to now. And I'm curious, as this musical goes through the preview process, what else they are going to adjust before it officially opens. Already from the first preview to now, we've gotten costume changes in the bows. The first night, one of the characters looked identical to Fiyero and now they've changed the colour of his pants. These are the kinds of changes that happen during a preview period, and I'm curious what other changes we'll see. I would love to see them adjust some of the scenic elements, especially the video elements. There are a couple moments that I feel like the staging could be bigger. There's definitely some sightline issues right now, so be aware, if you're sitting in the first five seats on either side, you're going to miss moments in the show, though. Those could be adjusted with some adjusting to the staging, and I definitely think that they could do a little bit of tightening, especially in the first act, to the writing overall. But there is definitely a lot to love about this show, especially the performances by Joy Woods and Jeremy Kushnier. And of course, it's Raúl Esparza’s big return to Broadway. As far as tickets go, I was invited to go see this, but you can get discounted tickets. There is both a digital lottery and an in person rush for $45. Not sure exactly where those seats are. They may be in those side seats, but for the most part, you can see everything. And I do think some of that staging could be adjusted to reduce the number of sightline issues. And Galileo officially opens on December 6th, so they have a while to continue to shape the show during previews. Cannot wait to see where the show ends up.
